revealed.theme: Sam keeps returning to the workshop: the hand that remembers what the head files and loses, a life proven by the marks it leaves, not by the labels put on it.

collisions.connection: All three cast the tenant as the suspect in their own life. 'protected from me' names it, 'proving negatives about a hallway' performs it, and live-1 makes 'evidence that I live there' the actual crime. Same itch: the system that houses you treats your presence as the threat.
collisions.question: If the flat's ideal tenant is one who leaves no trace at all, what exactly are you paying to do there?
collisions.extension: An hour of photographing scuffs you didn't make, so you can prove you weren't there in the one place you actually live.

collisions.connection: Dad 'never labelled anything... but knew where everything was'; the flatmate 'labelled her fridge shelf day one'. You landed the mechanism yourself in n08: 'we label the things we don't trust each other with'. The workshop ran on trust in the hands; the shared flat runs on labels because trust is gone.
collisions.question: Is a label always a small confession that the trust it replaces has already failed?
collisions.extension: Dad's whole workshop was one long unlabelled sentence only his hands could read; your fridge shelf needs a sticker because nobody in the flat can read anybody.

collisions.connection: 'characterful' about the mould and the wide-angle listing photos are the same move: language and lens conscripted to sell you a flat that doesn't exist. 'you're viewing the lens really' — and you're smelling the euphemism before the door opens.
collisions.question: Who is the fiction actually for — the buyer of the flat, or the person who has to keep saying the words?

eureka.why_now: live-1 arrived today and finally names the inverse of the workshop thread — a home where 'evidence that I live there is a chargeable offence' — completing months of notes about a life measured in the marks the hands leave behind.
eureka.question: If the workshop was nothing but a lifetime of unlabelled marks proving a man lived by hand, what does it do to you to rent a place where leaving any mark at all is damage?
eureka.extension: Dad's pencil, sharpened with a knife, left shavings everywhere and a knowledge nobody could bill him for; you stand in the hardware shop breathing sawdust for ten minutes because it's the only room left where being present isn't a deduction from your deposit.
